question.problem:
The inverse of the $2\times 2$ matrix $D$ is found using row operations, as shown below. Complete the process, and determine ${D}^{-1}.$

$$
\begin{aligned}[D\,|\,I\,] & =[\begin{aligned}-6 & 2 & 1 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=\frac{1}{2}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-3 & 1 & \frac{1}{2} & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & ↔{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 & 1 \\ -3 & 1 & \frac{1}{2} & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :=\text{___________} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 &  &  \\ 0 & 1 &  & \end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$
question.worked_solution:
We write down $D$ and the identity matrix $I$ side-by-side (as shown below) and apply the standard Gauss-Jordan method to transform the matrix $D$ into the identity matrix. We perform the same row operations on both matrices:

$$
\begin{aligned}[D\,|\,I\,] & =[\begin{aligned}-6 & 2 & 1 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=\frac{1}{2}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-3 & 1 & \frac{1}{2} & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & ↔{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 & 1 \\ -3 & 1 & \frac{1}{2} & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+3{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & \frac{1}{2} & 3\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The matrix ${D}^{-1}$ is given by the right-hand side of our big matrix after all of the transformations have been completed. Therefore, 

$$
{D}^{-1}=[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ \frac{1}{2} & 3\end{aligned}].
$$
